airports.name: Honolulu International Airport
airports.text: Honolulu International Airport is the main air gateway for Honolulu; compare transfer time with your hotel base before locking the first night.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Honolulu International Airport and central Honolulu before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Honolulu stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Honolulu hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Honolulu unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose City centre for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Honolulu International Airport, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

history.label: Origins
history.text: Honolulu is Hawaiian for 'sheltered harbor' or 'calm port'; this former meaning is also reflected in the related Māori cognate toponym Whangaruru in the tip of New Zealand's North Island.

history.label: 11th century
history.text: These indicate that there was a settlement where Honolulu now stands in the 11th century.
In November 1794, Captain William Brown of Great Britain was the first foreigner to sail into what is now Honolulu Harbor.

history.label: 19th century
history.text: The settlement grew from a handful of homes to a city in the early 19th century after Kamehameha I chose it as a replacement for his residence at Waikiki in 1810.
After Kamehameha I conquered Oʻahu in the Battle of Nuʻuanu at Nuʻuanu Pali, he moved his royal court from the Island of Hawaiʻi to Waikiki in 1804.
His court relocated in 1809 to what is now downtown Honolulu.
The capital was moved back to Kailua-Kona in 1812.
In 1845, Kamehameha III moved the permanent capital of the Hawaiian Kingdom from Lahaina on Maui to Honolulu.
Modern air travel brings, as of 2007, 7.6 million visitors annually to the islands, with 62.3% entering at Honolulu International Airport.
